title: Jodie Sweetin’s ‘Full House’ Star Reveals Shocking Money Crisis After Years of Drug Addiction – Page Six
body:
Jodie Sweetin, best known for her role as Stephanie Tanner on the iconic sitcom “Full House,” has opened up about the severe financial fallout from her decades‑long battle with substance abuse. Speaking candidly on Natanya Ross’s “We’re Still Here, Babe” podcast, the actress revealed that her addiction drained every penny she earned, leaving her “completely broke” and forcing her to confront a harsh new reality of humility and survival. Sweetin’s disclosure shines a light on the often‑overlooked economic toll of addiction, even for public figures whose careers appear glamorous from the outside.

The 39‑year‑old star recounted how, after years of intermittent sobriety and relapse, she found herself with no savings, no credit cards, and a bank account that read zero. “I was living on the edge, and the money just disappeared,” Sweetin said, describing how the cost of drugs, legal fees, and missed work opportunities compounded into a financial abyss. She explained that the situation escalated to the point where she had to rely on friends, family, and occasional odd jobs just to put food on the table. “I learned humility the hard way,” she added, noting that the experience forced her to reevaluate her priorities and rebuild her life from the ground up.

Industry insiders point out that Sweetin’s story is not unique among entertainers who grapple with addiction. The pressures of fame, erratic schedules, and easy access to substances can create a perfect storm for financial mismanagement. According to a 2023 study by the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), nearly 20 percent of individuals in the entertainment sector report significant debt linked to substance use, a figure that dwarfs the national average. Financial counselors who specialize in addiction recovery note that the stigma surrounding money troubles often prevents celebrities from seeking help early, prolonging the cycle of debt and dependence.

Despite the grim picture, Sweetin’s recent transparency marks a turning point in her recovery journey. She has been sober for over two years, a milestone she attributes to a combination of therapy, a strong support network, and a renewed focus on her craft. In recent months, she has returned to acting, landing guest spots on television dramas and participating in advocacy work for addiction recovery. Sweetin also announced plans to partner with a nonprofit that provides financial literacy workshops for individuals in recovery, aiming to address the “dual diagnosis” of substance abuse and fiscal instability.

Critics and fans alike have responded positively to Sweetin’s honesty, praising her for breaking the silence that often surrounds the monetary consequences of addiction. Social media commentary has highlighted how her story resonates with many who have faced similar hardships, sparking conversations about the need for comprehensive support systems that include both medical treatment and financial counseling. Mental health professionals stress that such public disclosures can reduce stigma and encourage others to seek help before financial ruin sets in.

Looking ahead, Sweetin hopes her experience will serve as both a cautionary tale and a beacon of hope. She emphasizes that recovery is an ongoing process that requires not only personal resolve but also structural changes within the entertainment industry to provide better resources for those struggling. As she continues to rebuild her career and financial stability, Sweetin’s journey underscores a broader cultural shift toward openness about the hidden costs of addiction, reminding audiences that behind the fame and fortune can lie a fragile human story in need of compassion and support.
